description: Registry of JavaScript frontend services for Playwright E2E evaluation. Consumed by resources/scripts/run-with-service.sh. Each entry declares how to build and start a local dev/preview server so the agent can explore the running UI and generate Playwright tests.

placeholders.${PORT}: HTTP port the server is launched on (default_port unless overridden via --service-port).

sample-js-app.description: Sample JavaScript frontend (Vite dev server) for Playwright E2E testing. Replace this entry with your actual project.
sample-js-app.notes: Vite dev server example. Adjust 'run' for other bundlers: Next.js uses 'npm run dev -- -p ${PORT}', Create React App uses 'PORT=${PORT} npm start'.

swup.description: swup page-transition library — static test fixture pages served at /.
swup.notes: Serves from tests/fixtures/ (serve.json sets public: tests/fixtures). The instrument step copies dist/ -> tests/fixtures/dist/ so the HTML pages can load Swup. Do NOT use --clear-tests with this project: the tests/ directory contains both test specs (tests/functional/) AND the app-serving config (tests/config/serve.json) and fixture pages (tests/fixtures/), so clearing tests/ would break the server startup. The existing Playwright config is at tests/config/playwright.config.ts; testDir is tests/functional/.

openplayerjs.description: OpenPlayerJS HTML5 media player — example HTML pages at /examples/.
build: node -e "const fs=require('fs');let w=fs.readFileSync('pnpm-workspace.yaml','utf8');w=w.replace('engineStrict: true','engineStrict: false').replace('unrs-resolver: set this to true or false','unrs-resolver: true');fs.writeFileSync('pnpm-workspace.yaml',w,'utf8')"
openplayerjs.notes: Serves from the repo root so importmap paths (./packages/*/dist/) in example HTML pages resolve correctly. Build patches package.json (removes strict engines field) and pnpm-workspace.yaml (sets engineStrict:false, approves unrs-resolver) before installing. The dist/ package artifacts are already staged from the host build, so 'pnpm run build' is skipped to save time. The existing Playwright config is playwright.config.ts; testDir is e2e/.

gridstack.description: gridstack.js drag-and-drop grid layout — interactive demo pages at /demo/.
gridstack.notes: default_port 8080 matches the playwright.config.ts baseURL (http://localhost:8080). Serves from the repo root so demo/ pages can resolve ../dist/gridstack-all.js. The dist/ artifacts are already staged from the host build; rebuild steps (grunt/webpack) are skipped. The existing Playwright config is playwright.config.ts; testDir is e2e/.

motion-vue.description: motion-vue Vue animation library — Vite playground at /.
motion-vue.notes: Starts the Vite dev server for the @motion-vue/playground-vite package. Health probe may need a few seconds while Vite compiles on first request. The existing Playwright config is playwright.config.ts; testDir is tests/.

The existing Playwright config is playwright.config.ts; testDir is e2e/.

hemmelig.description: Hemmelig.app — secret sharing, FULL STACK (Vite + Hono API mounted as middleware, Prisma/SQLite).
hemmelig.notes: Dependencies pre-installed. NOT frontend-only: vite.config mounts the Hono API through @hono/vite-dev-server (entry server.ts, everything not under /api excluded), so `npx vite` serves the frontend AND the backend. Two things were missing before, which together produced a result recorded as PHYSICAL_EFFECT_DID_NOT_OCCUR: DATABASE_URL is read from the ENVIRONMENT by the generated Prisma client at runtime (prisma.config.ts only supplies it to the CLI), and the instance is STATE-GATED -- a fresh database serves /setup 'Create Admin Account' and nothing else, so the secret surface is unreachable and no write can happen. Deterministic reset restores a baseline containing only the admin account via tools/hemmelig_reset.sh in the explorer repo; the repo's seed:demo is avoided because it inserts 216 secrets and 2733 analytics rows and uses Math.random(). health_path is /api/healthz so readiness proves the API half is up, not just the SPA shell. Persistence verified end to end: POST /api/secrets -> 201 with the secrets table going 0 -> 1.

bangle-io.description: Bangle.io — browser-local note application (IndexedDB + File System Access API).
bangle-io.notes: Dependencies pre-installed on host (pnpm workspace). Run from the browser-entry workspace package so Vite receives --host/--port directly: the `pnpm -r --filter ... -- --host` form does not pass them through, and Vite then binds IPv6 localhost only while the readiness gate polls 127.0.0.1. Persists to IndexedDB databases 'bangle-io-db', 'baby-idb-db-3', 'baby-idb-meta-3' plus a localStorage sync key; no backend. Deterministic reset means clearing those databases between runs. The app is STATE-GATED: with an empty database it renders only 'No workspace selected / Create a workspace to get started', so a prerequisite workspace is supplied through app.client_state_baseline (captured by tools/bangle_seed_state.py driving the app's own creation flow). base_path carries the app's hash route so the browser lands ON that workspace; the router is hash-based (/ws#route=ws-home&wsName=<name>), NOT the /ws/<name> path the ROUTES constants suggest. health_path stays / because the dev server serves the SPA shell at the root.

epic-stack.description: Epic Stack — full-stack React Router app (Prisma + SQLite, real server-side persistence).
epic-stack.notes: Dependencies pre-installed; `npm run build` + `prisma migrate deploy` + `prisma generate --sql` already run on host (the repo's own `setup` script also runs `playwright install`, which is not needed here). Persistence is Prisma -> SQLite at prisma/data.db; there is no external database service. MOCKS=true installs MSW handlers for FOUR EXTERNAL hosts only -- api.github.com/github.com (OAuth), api.pwnedpasswords.com, api.resend.com (email) and the Tigris S3 endpoint -- so the Prisma/SQLite path under measurement is untouched. The one persistence-relevant substitution is object storage for user/note images: the Tigris mock WRITES uploads to tests/fixtures/uploaded/ rather than suppressing them, so image persistence is relocated to the local filesystem, not lost. Deterministic reset restores a pristine seeded snapshot via tools/epic_stack_reset.sh in the explorer repo; the seed itself uses faker and is NOT reproducible, which is why a snapshot is restored instead of re-seeding. Authenticated surface: seeded admin user kody / kodylovesyou. The repo's own scripts wrap node in `cross-env`, which is a local devDependency and is NOT on PATH for the service shell (`cross-env: command not found`), so the environment is set through this entry's env block and the command is plain `node index.ts`; the server reads PORT from the environment (server/index.ts). Runs in PRODUCTION mode with a build performed as part of service start, which is AFTER witness instrumentation is applied -- so the probes are compiled into the bundle. This is also what makes witness verification work at all here: in dev mode the Vite middleware serves a CLIENT transform at each source path with server-only code stripped, so a server-side probe is reported MISSING and the run is refused; in production those source paths are not served, the verification falls back to the install-time attestation (service down when patched), and the probes are genuinely present.

keystone-blog.description: Keystone 6 usecase-blog example — GraphQL API + Admin UI over Prisma/SQLite.
keystone-blog.notes: Standalone example inside the Keystone monorepo; dependencies are installed at the repo root and the example resolves its Prisma client through the monorepo's `myprisma` alias (keystone.ts sets prismaClientPath). Shape under measurement: Admin UI -> GraphQL mutation -> Prisma -> SQLite at examples/usecase-blog/keystone-example.db. Three lists: Author, Post, Tag. No authentication (the auth examples are separate), so the whole surface is reachable without a session. `keystone dev` migrates on boot and rebuilds the Admin UI, so the first start is slow -- hence the long health timeout. Deterministic reset restores a pristine seeded snapshot via tools/keystone_blog_reset.sh in the explorer repo; seed-data.ts is itself reproducible (fixed authors/posts from examples/example-data.ts), so the snapshot is for speed and stability rather than to paper over randomness. `keystone dev` IGNORES a --port flag and reads PORT from the environment, which run-with-service.sh exports, so the port is passed as an explicit env assignment in the run command (PORT is substituted into the run string, not exported into its environment). Left in dev mode deliberately: there is nothing to instrument in this subject (the code that commits lives in @keystone-6/core under node_modules, not in application-owned source), so no witness spec is installed and the production-build ordering that epic-stack needs does not apply. repo_subdir is "." because the probe config points repo.input_dir directly at the example directory; naming the example again here would double the path.
